eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model guidance and climatological patterns position 38°C or higher as the leading outcome for Manila’s maximum temperature on May 28, reflecting the tail end of the hot-dry season when solar insolation peaks and urban heat-island effects amplify readings. PAGASA and international ensembles indicate mostly clear to partly cloudy skies with light winds ahead of monsoon onset, supporting strong daytime heating, while historical May maxima in the capital frequently reach 34–36°C and occasionally higher under similar conditions. Recent observations show afternoon highs near 35°C, with heat-index values already exceeding 42°C, consistent with trader emphasis on the upper end of the distribution. Key variables that could shift probabilities include any earlier arrival of scattered thunderstorms or changes in the next 48-hour forecast updates from official agencies.
